testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Pull out the air brake knob.

questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, press the brake pedal down.

questions.question: What condition should leaf springs be in?
questions.explanation: Leaf springs must not be broken. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing or broken, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: What is black ice like?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road looks wet underneath it. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive slowly and block other drivers?

options.text: Drive while using your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive while using your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you.

questions.question: What gauge shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: Which name does NOT refer to convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors. Flat side mirrors are not convex mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, air tanks, gauges, warning devices, brake pedal, foundation brakes, spring brakes, and parking brake controls. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: How can you avoid being an aggressive driver?

options.text: Plan trips without allocating extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Not make gestures to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make gestures to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning extra time for traffic, not tailgating, not driving slowly in the left lane, and not making gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test, a double combination vehicle should lose no more than 3 psi of air in one minute. If it loses more, something needs to be repaired and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what do both systems share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system use one air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. A dual system has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.

questions.question: If you get a speeding ticket in another state while driving your personal car, what should you do?

options.text: Not worry about your CDL being affected.
Notify the motor vehicle licensing agency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Notify the motor vehicle licensing agency.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer and your motor vehicle licensing agency about any traffic conviction within 30 days, even if it happened in another state and you were driving your own car. Parking tickets do not need to be reported.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. This prevents your brakes from wearing out too quickly.

questions.question: What should you check on the hoses of a vehicle with power steering?

options.text: To ensure that they are still clear.
To ensure that they are connected to the battery.
To ensure that they contain the proper amount of play.

questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for any leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see your vehicle when visibility is low?

options.text: Wave an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights to low beam during dawn, dusk, or other low-visibility times. If you have trouble seeing others, they have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: Stop safely away from the crash scene, wait for police to arrive, and describe the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does your braking distance change?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed, your braking distance increases by four times. Doubling speed from 20 to 40 mph multiplies braking distance by four.

questions.question: How often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator in cold weather?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. Check and refill it every day during cold weather.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle starts to hydroplane?

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Pull in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: What happens if you fail the air brakes endorsement test?

options.text: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Your CDL will have an air brake endorsement marked with an asterisk.
Your CDL will not be valid.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: If you do not pass the air brakes test, you cannot drive vehicles with air brakes.

questions.question: When driving a manual transmission vehicle, how can you stop it from rolling backward when you start from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop the vehicle from rolling backward, partly engage the clutch before you take your foot off the brake. Use the parking brake when needed to prevent rolling back.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good idea on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.
Is required so cargo stays supervised.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. These activities take your focus away from the road.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Is needed to warm up vehicle parts.

questions.explanation: Always speed up smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when you use your phone or do something with your hands.
Can happen when your mind wanders, like daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen when your mind wanders, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical ones. You can look at a hazard but not see it if you are thinking about something else.

questions.question: Bracing is used to:

options.text: Make items taller in a trailer.
Stop items from moving in a trailer.
Make items easier to unload from a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop items from moving in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking goes in the front, back, and sides of cargo. Bracing goes from the top of cargo to the floor and sides.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you tell if a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow light on the dashboard.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate inside the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow light on the dashboard.
questions.explanation: A vehicle with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) has a yellow ABS warning light on the dashboard.

questions.question: When construction workers are near the road, you should:
questions.explanation: In construction zones, do not go faster than the posted speed limit. Slow down more when workers are near the road.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, when should you inspect the load?

options.text: Only at the start of the drive.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.explanation: Check cargo and its securing devices before you start. During the trip, check them within the first 50 miles, every three hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: Are probably aware of the roadway.
May focus on repairs and not notice traffic nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: May focus on repairs and not notice traffic nearby.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people fixing a disabled vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on the repair work and not see oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drains in the air tanks to remove water and compressor oil. If these build up, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to prevent:

options.text: Ice from forming in the brake system.
People from breathing the air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems use an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: If your license is disqualified, you must:

options.text: Wait for your employer to be notified by the state.
Tell your employer within two business days.
Tell your employer within a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you cannot drive.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks in an air brake system. The air compressor governor controls it.

questions.question: After a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds when a vehicle starts. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Keep your vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not react to an aggressive driver's angry gestures. Do not make eye contact, as this may provoke them. Move out of their way if you can do so safely.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system applies and releases brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving normally.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, you should:

options.text: Check the load and securing devices after driving no more than 50 miles.
Not use your mirrors to look behind your vehicle.
Keep a cell phone in your hand for emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the load and securing devices after driving no more than 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Inspect cargo and securing devices before starting a trip. After you start driving, check the load within the first 50 miles, then every three hours or 150 miles, and after each break.

questions.question: If cargo on a flatbed trailer is 40 feet long, it needs at least:
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, use one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: When doing a parallel park, you should:

options.text: Back past the space, then pull forward into it.
Drive forward past the space, then back into it.
Drive forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a parallel park on the right side, drive forward past the space first. Then back your vehicle into it, keeping the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency brakes and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: If a train is approaching the railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across railroad tracks. It is hard to judge a train's speed correctly. When you see a train approaching, stop and wait for it to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: To know if a vehicle can carry a load safely, you should:

options.text: Know the tire rating for the front tires only.
Start driving and see if the vehicle handles well.

questions.explanation: It is your responsibility to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including the suspension system weight rating.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can allow poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can allow poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. It can let poisonous fumes enter the vehicle's cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: If you get a traffic violation conviction, you must tell your employer ____ of the conviction.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction while driving any vehicle. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Are usually blocked from moisture, so they cannot freeze.
Will stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sun and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection, you must be able to do all of the following about oil, except:

options.text: Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, you must show where the dipstick is, show that the oil level is safe, and show that the oil level is above the refill mark.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, you can:

options.text: Tap the brakes lightly several times before braking.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the driver's window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly several times before braking.
questions.explanation: Before slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you are about to slow down.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven at low speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is an addition to the regular braking system. It stops brakes from locking during hard braking. If ABS doesn't work, the basic brakes will still work, so you can drive and brake normally.
